name: Kuomintang in Burma
alt: Nationalist Chinese forces in the Shan State

predecessors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
predecessors.text: the village of Tachilek near Kengtung, where the KMT troops 'settled', and the ground 'between Kengtung City and Tachilek' held by March 1950: a 50 km circle at Tachileik cut to Shan State

successors.name: Union of Burma (Myanmar)
successors.text: the KMT's Shan territory 'between the Salween River on the west, the China border on the east, and Thailand on the south': the researcher's reading as a 100 km circle at Mong Hsat plus a 60 km circle…

ledger.x: 1949: Nationalist Chinese troops cross into Burma after the PLA enters Yunnan: 'began crossing into Burma in late December 1949 and early January 1950', settling 'at the village of Tachilek' near Kengtung.
1950: Burmese forces take Tachilek 'within weeks' of Burma's June 1950 demand that the KMT surrender or leave; the page gives no day.
1950: the KMT moves to Mong Hsat in July, its base for eleven years, 'about eighty miles from the Thai border'.
1950-07: the Burmese army contests the KMT's Mong Hsat base.
1952 (late): the KMT spreads over the eastern Shan country.
1961: the KMT leaves its Shan territory; the 450-700 who remained retreated into Thailand and Laos.
1961: the Nationalist army in Burma ends with the evacuation of 31 March to 17 April 1961; Li Mi had announced its dissolution on 30 May 1954, but about 6,000 irregulars stayed in Burma.

wars.name: Kuomintang insurgency in Burma
wars.outcome: Burma took Tachilek in 1950 and failed for two years to oust the KMT from Mong Hsat; the KMT spread over the Shan states in late 1952; Burma appealed to the UN in March 1953; the 1953-1954 evacuations to Taiwan left about 6,000 irregulars; joint Burmese-PLA…

certainty.note: An irregular army's zone with no recorded boundary; only Tachilek and Mong Hsat are named places.
